chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali ibn Asbat, from Sayf ibn 'Amirah, from Abdul A'la ibn Ayn, from Abu Abdillah (peace be upon him), who said:
He who believes in Allah and the Last Day should not sit in a gathering wherein an Imam is derogated or wherein a believer is faulted.
ai.seo_question: What is the condition for a believer regarding sitting in gatherings where Imams or other believers are criticized?
ai.summary: In Shia scholarship, this hadith from al-Kafi underscores the spiritual weight of social conduct, linking the integrity of one's faith directly to the preservation of the Imam's honor and the dignity of the community. It serves as a foundational principle for 'al-wala' wa al-barra' (affiliation and disaffiliation), warning that casual gatherings where religious authority is diminished can erode the believer's connection to the divine. This emphasizes that respect for the Imam is not merely ceremonial but a core component of 'Iman' (faith) itself.

en.hubeali:
Ali Bin Ibrahim, from his father, from Ali Bin Asbat, from Sayf Bin Ameyra, from Abdul A’ala Bin Ayn, 
(It has been narrated) from Abu Abdullah<sup>asws</sup> having said:
‘The one who believes in Allahazwj and the Last Day, so he should not sit in a gathering wherein an Imamasws is derogated (Taqseer), or wherein a Momin is faulted’.
en.sarwar: 9. Ali ibn Ibrahim has narrated from his father from Ali ibn Asbat from Sayf ibn ‘Amirah from ‘Abd al-‘Ala’ ibn ‘Ayun from abu ‘Abd Allah (a.s.) who has said the following: “
Whoever believes in Allah and in the Day of Judgment must not sit in a seat whereby an Imam is belittled or a believer is criticized.”
